title: SQLite datetime ORDER BY is wrong on mixed-storage columns: INTEGER-epoch rows always sort before ISO-TEXT rows
body:
Found while fixing #3912 (filter comparands vs. storage form). Same root cause family — a SQLite `Field.datetime` column is genuinely mixed-form — but a **different code path**, so it is not covered by that fix.

## Symptom

Sorting on a `Field.datetime` column ignores the instant whenever the column holds both storage forms. SQLite's type ordering is `NULL < INTEGER/REAL < TEXT < BLOB`, so **every** `Date`-written row sorts before **every** ISO-string-written row, regardless of when they actually happened.

## Repro

```ts
const d = new SqlDriver({ client: 'better-sqlite3', connection: { filename: ':memory:' }, useNullAsDefault: true });
await d.initObjects([{ name: 'p', fields: { at: { type: 'datetime' } } }]);

await d.create('p', { id: 'int-2026', at: new Date('2026-01-01T00:00:00Z') }); // INTEGER epoch
await d.create('p', { id: 'txt-2024', at: '2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z' });        // ISO TEXT

await d.find('p', { orderBy: [{ field: 'at', order: 'asc' }] });
// actual:   ['int-2026', 'txt-2024']
// expected: ['txt-2024', 'int-2026']
```

Verified on `claude/sqlite-datetime-filter-empty-hradlv` (i.e. **with** the #3912 fix applied), so this is independent of it.

## Why the mix exists

Exactly as documented in #3912: a JS `Date` binds as INTEGER epoch, while a REST/JSON write carries an ISO string (JSON has no `Date`) and a `defaultValue: 'NOW()'` slot stamps ISO TEXT. The platform's own `created_at` / `updated_at` are stamped as ISO strings (`sql-driver.ts:1329`/`:1364`) while being declared `datetime` (`packages/objectql/src/registry.ts:319`/`:340`), so any object that mixes seeded/imported rows with API-written rows is affected — and `created_at` is the default sort on a lot of list views.

## Blast radius beyond ordering

Cursor/keyset pagination built on a datetime sort key inherits the wrong order, so pages can skip or repeat rows rather than merely presenting them out of order.

## Fix direction

The same storage-form-aware treatment the other two paths now have — `sqliteTemporalArg` for bucketing (#3773) and `sqliteEpochMsSql` / `filterColumnExpr` for filters (#3912) — applied to the ORDER BY compilation. `SqlDriver.sqliteEpochMsSql` is already the shared normaliser and is directly reusable here.

Worth weighing as part of it: this trades index-ordered scans for an expression sort on SQLite datetime columns. The durable alternative is to stop producing the mix at all — normalise `Field.datetime` on write in `formatInput` (which currently leaves datetime untouched, `sql-driver.ts:4386`) plus a migration for existing TEXT rows — after which all three read paths could drop their CASE. That is a bigger change than either issue, but it is the one that removes the whole class.
